instantiated_cells.justification: Employer expenditure statements are filed with updated registration statements due the last day of January, May, and September (tri-annually), not annually.
The statute sets updated registration/expenditure filings for the last day of January, May, and September, not monthly.
The only periodic filing schedule specified is tri-annual (January/May/September), so no separate 'other' frequency is provided.
The statute requires filings three times per year (January/May/September), not quarterly (four times per year).
Updated registration and accompanying expenditure statements are due three times per year, not semi-annually.
Employers must file expenditure statements with updated registration statements due the last day of January, May, and September, i.e., tri-annually.
Employer registration requires name and business address (and real party in interest if different) but does not require stating whether the business is public or private.
Employer expenditure statements exclude 'compensation paid to legislative agents,' so direct lobbying costs as compensation are not required to be reported.
The employer filings require identification of bills/resolutions and expenditures, but do not require reporting each lobbying contact/communication.
The initial registration statement must include 'a brief description of the type of legislation' to which the engagement relates, reflecting general issues lobbied.
Employer expenditure statements must report expenditures (as defined to include items of value such as food, entertainment, lodging, and transportation) and their totals.
Employer statements must show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer (excluding office facilities and lobbyist compensation), which are indirect non-compensation costs.
The employer’s registration must list the legislative agent’s name, business address, and occupation, but nothing requires the employer to disclose the agent’s phone number.
Initial registration statements (filed by each employer) must include the name of the legislative agent and the name of the employer for each engagement.
No provision requires employers to disclose major financial contributors in their registration or expenditure statements.
Employer registration requires the employer’s 'name and business address' but does not require a phone number.
Updated registration statements must list 'the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated' during the covered period.
An employer’s statement must show the 'total amount of expenditures made by the employer' during the reporting period.
Because employer expenditure statements expressly exclude 'compensation paid to legislative agents,' employers are not required to include salary/fees paid to lobbyists.

When expenditures are made for/on behalf of particular covered officials (and meals above $50 for agents), the statement must include the recipient name, amount, description, and approximate date—an itemized format.
For trade associations/charitable or fraternal organizations, the employer need not list each member, and no requirement exists to list sponsors/members.
Employer registration statements must identify the legislative agent(s) engaged by the employer, thereby listing lobbyists employed/retained.
